items.title: Onaje Allan Gumbs interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 12, 2001
items.q: He, Cal Tjader and Gabor Szabo. Unfortunately all three of them have passed away.

ctx.x: Yeah they didn’t announce it or it just went by real fast. Because we did a composition that I had written that I had never done arranging before either. So they helped me orchestrate this tune and we did it. And so he opened the letter. Not only did he open the letter, he Xeroxed the letter and put the letter on the bulletin board, so everybody could read this letter that was mailed to me. I’m in theory class and they say, “Allan, man” there was a guy, Joe Pizano I think his name was, “there’s a letter for you…

Herbie Hancock. Now mind you he’s only like all of twenty something years old, but to me he was like this legend, and he’s still in his twenties. But I got to know him and really it was an incredible situation, but while I was in college, Billy Taylor, Dr. Billy Taylor, afforded me the opportunity to arrange — compose and arrange — some music for a show he was the musical director of at that time, that was David Frost. And I had gone to him and said I’d like to write something for the show. And he said well come…
